title: Avoiding Sanitary Tees in Horizontal Drainage Runs
description: Installing a standard sanitary tee on a horizontal-to-horizontal drain line is a frequent code violation and installation error. Sanitary tees have a short sweep designed primarily for vertical-to-horizontal directional changes or vent connections. When used horizontally, the abrupt turn restricts flow, leads to solids catching, and increases clogging potential. Drainage standards require a combination wye and eighth bend or a long-sweep wye for horizontal direction changes. Using the correct directional fitting ensures smooth waste flow, proper venting airflow, and easier drain cleaning access for cables without damaging pipe walls.

Avoiding Sanitary Tees in Horizontal Drainage Runs

Installing a standard sanitary tee on a horizontal-to-horizontal drain line is a frequent code violation and installation error. Sanitary tees have a short sweep designed primarily for vertical-to-horizontal directional changes or vent connections. When used horizontally, the abrupt turn restricts flow, leads to solids catching, and increases clogging potential. Drainage standards require a combination wye and eighth bend or a long-sweep wye for horizontal direction changes. Using the correct directional fitting ensures smooth waste flow, proper venting airflow, and easier drain cleaning access for cables without damaging pipe walls.
